name: Dodge M4S Turbo Interceptor Concept
description:
The Dodge M4S Turbo Interceptor is a unique concept car created by Chrysler Corporation's design team in the early 1980s. Built on a heavily modified chassis, this mid-engine exotic featured radical styling that would become iconic through its starring role in the 1986 film 'The Wraith'. The M4S showcased advanced aerodynamic design with its wedge-shaped profile, scissor doors, and futuristic aesthetics that pushed the boundaries of automotive design.

Powered by a turbocharged 2.2-liter four-cylinder engine producing approximately 440 horsepower, the M4S demonstrated impressive performance capabilities despite its experimental nature. The car featured a unique semi-automatic transmission and rear-wheel drive layout. With its lightweight construction and advanced aerodynamics, the M4S was capable of exceeding 300 km/h, making it one of the fastest concept cars of its era.

While only a handful of M4S prototypes were built and it never reached production, the Dodge M4S Turbo Interceptor remains a significant piece of automotive history, representing an era of bold experimentation in American automotive design.
